title: Slowly growing multiway systems eventually become repetitive

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Slowly growing multiway systems eventually become repetitive

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Even when slowly growing multiway systems show early apparent randomness in their state counts, they typically end up showing some form of repetition (sometimes with long periods, such as 1071 steps).

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: even when such growth leads to a certain amount of apparent randomness it typically in the end seems to exhibit some form of repetition.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 5, “Two Dimensions and Beyond”; section “Multiway Systems” (from p. 204), p. 207. Scope: slowly growing multiway systems

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch05-13: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.60

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Periodicity and growth can be defined precisely after interpretive choices, and simulations can cover many small systems. Existing computation cannot establish the open-ended typicality and eventuality as stated.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Enumerate bounded simple multiway systems with subexponential state-count growth and test their count sequences for eventual periodicity up to increasing horizons. Counterexamples within the enumerated class refute the bounded version, while confirmation remains horizon-dependent.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
“Typically” lacks a rule-sampling distribution.

Long transients can mimic nonperiodicity.

No finite simulation proves eventual repetition.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.42
analysis feasibility: 0.62
discriminating power: 0.58
data existence: 0.85
operationalizability: 0.48

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The period-1071 example is a concrete simulation with the rule given in the text, and repetition of a count sequence is a sharp detection problem. Typically and in the end still refer to an open collection of slowly growing systems, and failure to find a cycle does not refute an unbounded wait. A sample can confirm the published example and estimate a rate; it cannot close the general statement.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For each slowly growing rule, track the sequence of string counts and test whether it becomes periodic, including the stated period-1071 example. A cycle supports the example; a diverse sample that stays aperiodic past many times its apparent transient would challenge the word typically.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Apparent randomness has to be translated into a chosen statistical test.

Periods of hundreds or thousands of steps are missed by short runs.

Eventually is not a finite test: a cycle can sit beyond any chosen cutoff.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

analysis feasibility: 0.55
data existence: 0.68
